reviews.coverage: All 17 slides visually inspected at 2048px on 26 October 2026. Useful broad account and readable layouts; generated diagrams need the corrections below. Original retained for review.
findings: Slide 4 describes rdfs:domain as a prohibition on use outside a class. RDFS domain supports type inference; SHACL supplies the explicit data constraints.

Slide 5 is not a faithful model diagram: Address belongs to property-data-services, hasAddress links Property to Address, and postcode is text on Address. The illustrated hasAddress-to-Active, postcode-to-utilityOutcome and invented common:Owner links must not be used as model guidance.
Slides 8 and 11 turn conditional requiredness into a third answer value. Source item pp-0067a00fc9eb permits Yes and No; conditional describes when the answer is required.
Slide 7 reverses the useful relationship: Property hasUtilityServiceRecord UtilityServiceRecord. Slide 8 gives the correct overall direction.
Slide 11 implies a universal mandatory source-evidence constraint for the sewer-map item; consult its exact coverage/source constraints instead.
Slide 14 uses SW1A, an incomplete UK postcode, as its passing illustration. The simplified candidate constraint checks postcode presence; this is not proof of a valid real-world postcode.
Slide 15 conflates RDF parsing with SHACL constraint evaluation. Parsing, validation and factual verification are distinct checks.
Slide 2 calls the model one singular truth. This is a draft candidate; its coverage and validation do not establish factual correctness.

reviews.coverage: Complete landscape infographic visually inspected. Clear ownership-versus-reuse contrast, useful direct-cross-domain explanation and readable hierarchy.
findings: The page supplies the candidate status omitted by the image. The eight homes comprise six domain contexts, the DBT scheme and common; they are not eight business domains.
The concise common description emphasises shared identity; the complete source also covers stable shared exchange meaning.
